deepdive.sec: FMCG / Edible Oils & Ayurvedic Wellness Products

bull_bear.body: Focus on brand building (ATL ad spend INR64cr in Q1), distribution expansion (rural Gramin Mitra, Gramin Arogya Kendras), D2C (Order Me app, website), and HPC/nutraceutical innovation; no M&A active; organic growth prioritized over acquisitions
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Government intervention in staples (price controls, stock declarations); volatility in butter/palm oil prices; urban demand recovery slower than expected; margin compression from alternate channel competition; D2C scale still minimal (<1%)
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, strategic, and disciplined; focused on long-term margin expansion (8-10% FMCG, 4% edible oils), willing to sacrifice low-margin staple sales; optimistic on HPC/nutraceutical growth and duty cut tailwinds; clear 50-50 revenue split target (FMCG:edible oils) by 2030
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Oil palm plantation revenue doubled to INR592cr — a strategic long-term asset with 43.4% of plantation in prime yielding age; D2C is growing at 40% despite being <1% of revenue; 70% of e-commerce is quick commerce; 35-40% of India’s paddy is government procured, creating structural headwinds for staples
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- integration: backward integration from farmer-led oil palm cultivation and milling into refining and branded oils — evidence: 1,10,722 hectares under oil palm cultivation across 12 States, six oil mills with aggregate capacity of 1.15 Mn MTs, and domestic plantation procurement contributed approximately 10.9% import substitution in FY 2025-26 — against it: management states near-term Edible Oils performance 'remains influenced by commodity cycles'
- resource: runway of allocated oil palm development area well beyond the area planted — evidence: 6.63 lakh hectares allocated for oil palm development, #1 in India by allocated area (company's own estimate), versus 1,10,722 hectares under cultivation
- brand: category leadership in branded soya protein — evidence: Nutrela holds ~40% market share in branded soya chunks, mini chunks and granules (company's estimate) with a 35+ year legacy
- distribution: owned/franchise retail network on top of general trade — evidence: 434 Mega Stores, 1,063 Chikitsalayas, 2,142 Arogya Kendras and 1,822 Grameen Arogya Kendras, plus 8,000+ distributors, 84 super distributors, 96 depots and 2 Million+ retail touchpoints
- scale: multi-site edible oil processing footprint — evidence: 26 manufacturing locations including 7 refineries, 7 integrated plants, 3 seed-crushing and 3 palm-crushing units; branded edible oils ~75% of Edible Oils segment sales — against it: management states near-term segment performance remains influenced by commodity cycles, import duty changes and palm/soyabean price movements
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Commodity price volatility — The Company's financial risk framework names commodity price fluctuations as a core exposure, managed under a Board-approved Commodity Price Risk Management Policy via futures, sale contracts and supply arrangements; input-cost movements are flagged in the strategic outlook.
- Foreign currency exposure on imports and exports — Foreign currency movements on import and export exposures are a named financial risk, hedged through forward and futures contracts under a Board-approved Foreign Exchange Risk Management Policy.
- Interest rate variations — Interest rate variations are listed alongside commodity and currency exposures in the Company's financial risk management framework.
- Export competitiveness of Indian soya products — Exports declined during the year due to intense international competition and the higher cost of Indian soya products relative to other international suppliers.
- Related-party transaction compliance — The secretarial auditor observed that a wholly owned subsidiary paid an advance to a related party without audit committee approval (Reg. 23(2) LODR); the advance was returned and the Company has filed a settlement application with SEBI.
- Macroeconomic, geopolitical and regulatory change — The ERM framework identifies macroeconomic conditions, geopolitical developments, regulatory changes, technological advancements and climate-related considerations as influences on the operating environment; the outlook names regulatory developments and geopolitical uncertainties as watch-items.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Edible oils: INR6,685cr revenue (+25% YoY), 72% branded, EBITDA 1.78%; HPC: INR639cr revenue, EBITDA 18.7% (Dant Kanti led growth, exported to 9 countries); Food & FMCG: INR1,661cr revenue (-15% YoY), EBITDA 5.23%; Biscuits: INR451cr revenue, 9.2% EBITDA; Nutrela: INR140cr revenue, 14.5% EBITDA; Nutraceuticals: INR17cr revenue, turned positive EBITDA; Oil palm: INR592cr revenue (doubled), 92,133ha cultivated; Staples: INR616cr revenue, flat EBITDA
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body: Patanjali Foods has moved from an edible-oil-led business into a broader FMCG company: it refines, crushes and markets branded edible oils, vanaspati and bakery fats, runs a farmer-led oil palm plantation and milling programme and an oleochemicals business, and sells foods, biscuits, textured soya protein (Nutrela), nutraceuticals and home & personal care products. It serves households across urban and rural India through general trade, its own franchise store network (Mega Stores, Chikitsalayas, Arogya Kendras), modern retail and digital channels, alongside institutional (HoReCa, defence canteens, state civil supplies) and bakery customers. It also generates wind power for captive consumption and grid supply.

business.body:
- **Edible Oils:** Ruchi Gold, Mahakosh, Sunrich, Ruchi Star, Ruchi No. 1, Tulsi Gold, Soyumm, Nutrela, Patanjali, palmolein, soyabean oil, sunflower oil, mustard oil, Yellow Mustard Oil (new launch), vanaspati, speciality and bakery fats, shortenings, hydrogenated fats
- **Oil Palm Plantation:** Fresh Fruit Bunch procurement and milling, domestic crude palm oil
- **Oleochemicals:** soap noodles, castor derivatives, split fatty acid, refined glycerine
- **FMCG - Food:** biscuits, cookies, rusk, noodles, breakfast cereals, Nutrela honey, Nutrela high-protein atta, Nutrela premium edible oils
- **FMCG - Textured Soya Protein:** Nutrela soya chunks, mini chunks, granules
- **FMCG - Nutraceuticals:** general nutrition, sports nutrition, medical nutrition (vegetarian focus)
- **FMCG - Home and Personal Care:** home and personal care products
- **Wind Turbine Power Generation:** renewable power for captive consumption, grid supply

outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: HPC premiumization (Dant Kanti Advanced, Sensitive, Aloe Vera); Nutraceuticals expansion (10-12 new SKUs); D2C channel scaling (currently <1% revenue, growing 40%); Oil palm plantation (long-term margin driver); Export expansion (Dant Kanti in 9 countries)
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Consolidate FMCG (including the integrated Home and Personal Care business) with edible oils into a balanced growth engine; after the first full year of HPC integration, shift HPC from consolidation to acceleration through product innovation, wider distribution and brand visibility.
- Move over the medium term towards a more equal revenue contribution between the oil and FMCG businesses, intended to reduce earnings volatility and improve margin quality.
- Keep expanding edible oil capacity and the oil palm plantation programme across 12 States under NMEO-OP as backward integration.
- Distribution is a core pillar: build presence across General Trade, Modern Trade, E-commerce and emerging digital channels, extending the 2 million+ outlet direct retail footprint.
- Leverage the Ayurvedic heritage playbook: premiumisation as the anchor for alternate channels, and export-led initiatives for Ayurveda-led natural product lines.
- Stated strategic priorities: focus on high-margin stable businesses and maintain strategic alignment to Health, Wellness and Ayurveda.
- Climate approach: pursue carbon neutrality progressively plant-by-plant and asset-by-asset using owned wind/renewable assets and oil palm carbon sinks rather than purchased offsets, with net zero as a longer-term ambition aligned to India's 2070 path.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Expansion is centred on the oil palm programme: planted area reached 1,10,722 hectares across 12 States during FY 2025-26 (up from 89,546 ha), out of 6.63 lakh ha allocated for future expansion, supported by six oil palm mills with an aggregate capacity of 1.15 Mn MTs. Commercial production commenced at the oil palm mill in Arunachal Pradesh during the year (the climate table separately cites commencement of commercial production at the oil palm mill in Niglok). Plantation-related investment went into nurseries across States and off-grid solar at plantation nurseries. On the environmental side, the Company operates 7 Zero Liquid Discharge plants with 2 more in the pipeline, runs 84.6 MW of installed wind capacity (60.85 MW operational) across 16 locations in 6 States, and has a 0.50 MW captive solar plant while expanding solar adoption. The Directors' Report states the Company 'continues to strategically expand capacity and reinforce its leadership in edible oils'.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Edible oil business expected to grow in line with underlying industry demand, supported by a stable consumption environment and a supportive operating environment.
- Foods portfolio growth expected to outpace the core oils business; margins expected to improve gradually, led by normalisation in Foods.
- Efficiency gains expected in HPC from full integration with the parent business.
- Exports declined in FY26 due to intense international competition and the higher cost of Indian soya products versus other international suppliers.
- Industry demand narrative: shift from loose to branded and packaged staples, premium and health-focused consumption, e-commerce and quick-commerce expansion into tier-2/3 cities, and rising plant-protein adoption.
- Government support through the National Mission on Edible Oils is cited as boosting domestic oil palm cultivation, with India's edible oil demand still heavily met by imports.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Revenue grew 24% YoY on strong rural demand and HPC growth, but margins were pressured by high raw material costs and inventory markdowns from recent duty cuts; key improvement catalysts are normalized palm oil pricing and full benefit from ghee price hikes in Q2, driving path to 8-10% FMCG EBITDA margin and 4% edible oil margin by FY26

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Diversified Indian consumer company spanning edible oils, foods, nutrition and home & personal care, backed by an integrated domestic oil palm plantation programme across 12 States.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Patanjali Foods has moved from an edible-oil-led business into a broader FMCG company: it refines, crushes and markets branded edible oils, vanaspati and bakery fats, runs a farmer-led oil palm plantation and milling programme and an oleochemicals business, and sells foods, biscuits, textured soya protein (Nutrela), nutraceuticals and home & personal care products. It serves households across urban and rural India through general trade, its own franchise store network (Mega Stores, Chikitsalayas, Arogya Kendras), modern retail and digital channels, alongside institutional (HoReCa, defence canteens, state civil supplies) and bakery customers. It also generates wind power for captive consumption and grid supply.

products.body:

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Edible oil business expected to grow in line with underlying industry demand, supported by a stable consumption environment and a supportive operating environment.
- Foods portfolio growth expected to outpace the core oils business; margins expected to improve gradually, led by normalisation in Foods.
- Efficiency gains expected in HPC from full integration with the parent business.
- Exports declined in FY26 due to intense international competition and the higher cost of Indian soya products versus other international suppliers.
- Industry demand narrative: shift from loose to branded and packaged staples, premium and health-focused consumption, e-commerce and quick-commerce expansion into tier-2/3 cities, and rising plant-protein adoption.
- Government support through the National Mission on Edible Oils is cited as boosting domestic oil palm cultivation, with India's edible oil demand still heavily met by imports.

capital_allocation.body: Focus on brand building (ATL ad spend INR64cr in Q1), distribution expansion (rural Gramin Mitra, Gramin Arogya Kendras), D2C (Order Me app, website), and HPC/nutraceutical innovation; no M&A active; organic growth prioritized over acquisitions

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Expansion is centred on the oil palm programme: planted area reached 1,10,722 hectares across 12 States during FY 2025-26 (up from 89,546 ha), out of 6.63 lakh ha allocated for future expansion, supported by six oil palm mills with an aggregate capacity of 1.15 Mn MTs. Commercial production commenced at the oil palm mill in Arunachal Pradesh during the year (the climate table separately cites commencement of commercial production at the oil palm mill in Niglok). Plantation-related investment went into nurseries across States and off-grid solar at plantation nurseries. On the environmental side, the Company operates 7 Zero Liquid Discharge plants with 2 more in the pipeline, runs 84.6 MW of installed wind capacity (60.85 MW operational) across 16 locations in 6 States, and has a 0.50 MW captive solar plant while expanding solar adoption. The Directors' Report states the Company 'continues to strategically expand capacity and reinforce its leadership in edible oils'.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, strategic, and disciplined; focused on long-term margin expansion (8-10% FMCG, 4% edible oils), willing to sacrifice low-margin staple sales; optimistic on HPC/nutraceutical growth and duty cut tailwinds; clear 50-50 revenue split target (FMCG:edible oils) by 2030

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- integration: backward integration from farmer-led oil palm cultivation and milling into refining and branded oils — evidence: 1,10,722 hectares under oil palm cultivation across 12 States, six oil mills with aggregate capacity of 1.15 Mn MTs, and domestic plantation procurement contributed approximately 10.9% import substitution in FY 2025-26 — against it: management states near-term Edible Oils performance 'remains influenced by commodity cycles'
- resource: runway of allocated oil palm development area well beyond the area planted — evidence: 6.63 lakh hectares allocated for oil palm development, #1 in India by allocated area (company's own estimate), versus 1,10,722 hectares under cultivation
- brand: category leadership in branded soya protein — evidence: Nutrela holds ~40% market share in branded soya chunks, mini chunks and granules (company's estimate) with a 35+ year legacy
- distribution: owned/franchise retail network on top of general trade — evidence: 434 Mega Stores, 1,063 Chikitsalayas, 2,142 Arogya Kendras and 1,822 Grameen Arogya Kendras, plus 8,000+ distributors, 84 super distributors, 96 depots and 2 Million+ retail touchpoints
- scale: multi-site edible oil processing footprint — evidence: 26 manufacturing locations including 7 refineries, 7 integrated plants, 3 seed-crushing and 3 palm-crushing units; branded edible oils ~75% of Edible Oils segment sales — against it: management states near-term segment performance remains influenced by commodity cycles, import duty changes and palm/soyabean price movements

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Government intervention in staples (price controls, stock declarations); volatility in butter/palm oil prices; urban demand recovery slower than expected; margin compression from alternate channel competition; D2C scale still minimal (<1%)

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Oil palm plantation revenue doubled to INR592cr — a strategic long-term asset with 43.4% of plantation in prime yielding age; D2C is growing at 40% despite being <1% of revenue; 70% of e-commerce is quick commerce; 35-40% of India’s paddy is government procured, creating structural headwinds for staples

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Consolidate FMCG (including the integrated Home and Personal Care business) with edible oils into a balanced growth engine; after the first full year of HPC integration, shift HPC from consolidation to acceleration through product innovation, wider distribution and brand visibility.
- Move over the medium term towards a more equal revenue contribution between the oil and FMCG businesses, intended to reduce earnings volatility and improve margin quality.
- Keep expanding edible oil capacity and the oil palm plantation programme across 12 States under NMEO-OP as backward integration.
- Distribution …

themes.title: Consumption revival & FMCG premiumization
themes.need: Rural recovery, GST 2.0 and premiumization still frame the theme, but Q1FY27 rewarded portfolio SHAPE over volume. TATACONSUM's growth businesses hit INR 1,300cr (+47%) and are now 36% of India - larger than either salt (>INR 1,000cr) or tea & coffee (INR 1,200cr), with Sampann +58%, RTD +41% and Capital Foods INR 232cr (+40%) - while India tea revenue fell 4% on +2% volume as lower tea costs were deliberately passed back (tea inflation is now running 7-10% with most buying still ahead, so that inverts next year). PGHH shows the margin route: FY26 sales roughly flat at ~INR 4,300cr but PAT +19% to ~INR 850cr and ~100bps of structural margin from INR 86cr of productivity savings, absorbing crude and resin each up 30-50% with no stock-outs. The cautionary tale is licensed brands - JYOTHYLAB lost the Pril and Fa licences when Henkel did not renew (all manufacturing and selling stopped 1-June; Pril was ~7-8% of revenue, ~INR 225-240cr) and has filed SIAC arbitration. MARICO/DABUR/GODREJCP/COLPAL/EMAMILTD ride distribution + premium mix; VBL on beverage route-to-market; BIKAJI/GOPAL/BECTORFOOD on branded snacks; ORKLAINDIA took a 4% blended price increase in Q4 plus premium mix to a 16.9% EBITDA margin.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull-through; rural volume recovery; festive/wedding restocking; commodity pass-back timing; JYOTHYLAB's ~7-8% revenue hole and the SIAC arbitration.
